title: A frozen two-component size fit gives no clear NICER gain for 23 PSR J0537-6910 glitches
abstract: We test whether a size density with two components transfers from 45 RXTE glitches to 23 NICER glitches of PSR J0537-6910. A lognormal plus positive Gaussian fit gives a total NICER log score gain of 0.0228 over a single positive Gaussian. The mean gain is 0.0010 per event. Its fixed-fit two-event block resampling range is -0.111 to +0.151. A training and test resampling check also includes zero. Removal of the sole NICER event below 50 catalog size units changes the mean gain to -0.0602. The mixture improves on a single lognormal, but this does not establish two physical mechanisms. Models use normalized event likelihoods and fixed RXTE parameters. Different instruments reduce one source of artifact, but timing methods, missing small events, size errors, detection limits and epoch changes remain limits. This is a retrospective transfer test, not a new glitch detection. The package contains code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and a figure. External catalog rows remain outside the baseline publication. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-a6da0da7f162; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: RXTE fits and NICER predictive gains. Error bars use fixed-fit circular blocks of two events. The primary positive Gaussian contrast includes zero.

citations.reason: Motivates a transfer test of a lognormal plus Gaussian size density. We do not reproduce the original parameters or sample.
Prior report supplies the instrument split; our outcome is size density, not waiting time.
